boundary.internal: Scope-aware proven-receiver dataflow (nested shadow + inner class + rebind)

api.name: walkForCalls
api.signature: function walkForCalls(node: SyntaxNode, callerId: string, repo: string, filePath: string, relations: Relation[], seen: Set<string>, axiosScopes: Set<string>[]): void

parameters.name: callerId
parameters.purpose: entity id of the enclosing function/method (CALLS_HTTP.from)

parameters.name: relations
parameters.purpose: accumulator the recognizer pushes CALLS/CALLS_HTTP into

parameters.name: axiosScopes
parameters.purpose: REPLACES the old flat `localHttp: Set<string>` param: a stack of per-lexical-scope axios-var proof frames (innermost last). A receiver is proven iff the nearest frame that declares the name proves it as an axios.create var; a nearer non-axios declaration of the same name shadows it. On entering a function/arrow/method scope, push that scope's collectLocalAxiosVars(scope) frame and pop on exit; captured (not re-declared) outer axios vars still resolve via an outer frame.

returns.meaning: mutates `relations` in place; emits at most one CALLS_HTTP per proven receiver call-site

preconditions: axiosScopes contains one frame per enclosing lexical scope from outermost to innermost
postconditions: A `<recv>.<verb>(url)` emits CALLS_HTTP only when isHttpVerb(verb) AND (currentClassHttpFields.has(recv) for the NEAREST enclosing class OR recv resolves to an axios proof in its nearest declaring scope frame)
A receiver whose name is re-declared (shadowed) by a non-axios binding in a nearer scope does NOT emit

On entering a class/class_declaration node, currentClassHttpFields is saved, set to that inner class's collectClassHttpFields, and restored on exit (so a method-body-declared inner class no longer inherits the outer class's this.<field> proof)

api.name: collectLocalAxiosVars

parameters.name: scope
parameters.purpose: a single lexical scope node (function/arrow/method body) whose DIRECTLY-declared axios.create vars are collected

returns.meaning: names declared by `const x = axios.create(...)` directly within this scope; the DFS stops at nested function/arrow scope boundaries so each scope owns its own frame (mirrors collectClassHttpFields stopping at nested class boundaries)

postconditions: A name declared in a nested inner scope is NOT included in the outer scope's frame
Only axios.create declarators contribute; a same-named non-axios declarator in this scope does not add the name (and, being the nearest frame, shadows an outer proof at resolution time)

api.name: collectPyProvenHttpReceivers

parameters.name: root
parameters.purpose: the function subtree whose requests.Session()/httpx.Client() proofs are collected

returns.meaning: names PROVEN HTTP clients under last-binding-wins: a name whose LAST assignment in the subtree is the factory is proven; a name later reassigned with a non-factory RHS is removed

postconditions: A proven name reassigned with a non-factory RHS later in the same function drops out of the set
A name whose final binding is the factory stays proven even if an earlier binding was non-factory

api.name: walkPythonForHttpCalls
api.signature: function walkPythonForHttpCalls(root: SyntaxNode, callerId: string, repo: string, filePath: string, relations: Relation[]): void

returns.meaning: unchanged signature; consumes the corrected (rebind-aware) proven set from collectPyProvenHttpReceivers

postconditions: A `<obj>.<verb>(url)` emits CALLS_HTTP only when obj is in the rebind-corrected proven set

dataModel.details: No shape change to the CALLS_HTTP relation (kind/from/to/resolved/meta unchanged). The EMISSION invariant is tightened: an instance-client CALLS_HTTP is minted only when the receiver resolves to a proof in its NEAREST lexical scope (axios var frame or nearest-class this.<field>), and in Python only when the receiver's final binding is a factory. Strictly narrows false positives; never widens.

dataModelChanges.details: No shape change to the CALLS_HTTP relation (kind/from/to/resolved/meta unchanged). The EMISSION invariant is tightened: an instance-client CALLS_HTTP is minted only when the receiver resolves to a proof in its NEAREST lexical scope (axios var frame or nearest-class this.<field>), and in Python only when the receiver's final binding is a factory. Strictly narrows false positives; never widens.

errorCases.scenario: A scope/class node lacks the expected child fields (e.g. childForFieldName('type')/('name')/('value')/('function') returns null on an incomplete or error node)
errorCases.detection: The optional-chained field reads (`typeNode`, `nameNode`, `value?.type`, `fn?.text`) evaluate to null/undefined and the guard is false
errorCases.response: Skip that binding — do not add a proof, do not emit; continue the walk (fail-closed, no throw)
errorCases.userImpact: The one ambiguous call-site is simply not recognized as HTTP; no crash, no bogus edge

errorCases.scenario: axiosScopes stack underflow — a receiver referenced with no enclosing scope frame pushed (e.g. top-level module code)
errorCases.detection: The resolution loop finds no frame declaring the name; the stack may be empty
errorCases.response: Treat as unproven (no frame proves it) — emit nothing rather than throwing on an empty stack
errorCases.userImpact: Top-level (non-function) axios usage that was never in scope of the local-var proof is unaffected — same as today

edgeCases.input: Outer `const client = axios.create()`; a nested callback does `arr.forEach(() => client.get(url))` WITHOUT re-declaring client
edgeCases.expected: Emits one CALLS_HTTP — the closure captures the outer axios var; no nearer frame shadows `client`, so it resolves to the outer axios proof

edgeCases.input: Outer `const client = axios.create()`; a nested callback does `arr.forEach(() => { const client = new Map(); client.get(k); })`
edgeCases.expected: No CALLS_HTTP for the nested `client.get` — the inner scope frame declares `client` (non-axios), shadowing the outer proof at its nearest declaration

edgeCases.input: Same body: outer `client.get(url)` (axios) AND a nested shadow `const client = new Map(); client.get(k)`
edgeCases.expected: Exactly one CALLS_HTTP — for the outer axios call only; the nested shadowed read does not emit (outer capture preserved, inner shadow subtracted)

edgeCases.input: class Outer { constructor(private http: HttpClient){} m(){ class Inner { http = new Map(); go(){ return this.http.get('k'); } } } }
edgeCases.expected: No CALLS_HTTP for Inner.go — entering the Inner class node saves+switches currentClassHttpFields to Inner's (empty) set; restored to Outer's on exit

edgeCases.input: class Outer { constructor(private http: HttpClient){} m(){ return this.http.get('https://api/x'); class Inner { http = new Map(); } } }
edgeCases.expected: One CALLS_HTTP — Outer.m's this.http.get still emits (Outer frame active); the inner class declaration does not disturb the outer proof after restore
One CALLS_HTTP — for the first `s.get` while the final binding logic must still credit the factory-proven use; the post-rebind `s.get('k')` (dict) does not emit

edgeCases.input: Python: `s = {}; s = requests.Session(); s.get('https://a')` (proven is the FINAL binding)
edgeCases.expected: One CALLS_HTTP — last-binding-wins keeps `s` proven because its final assignment is the factory

edgeCases.input: A receiver named like an axios var but never declared in any enclosing scope (free/imported identifier)
edgeCases.expected: No CALLS_HTTP — unproven; unchanged from today

invariantsToPreserve.text: The Angular `this.http.get(url)` HttpClient-DI happy path still emits exactly one CALLS_HTTP with the raw URL for the class that actually declares an HttpClient-typed field/ctor-param.
The `const c = axios.create(); c.post(url)` local-instance happy path still emits one CALLS_HTTP when c is not shadowed.
An unproven receiver (`foo.get`, `new Map().get`, a param named http typed as SomethingElse) still emits ZERO CALLS_HTTP.
Python `s = requests.Session(); s.get(url)` / `httpx.Client()` happy path still emits one CALLS_HTTP.

emitCallsHttp still pushes exactly one unresolved CALLS_HTTP per proven call-site and skips an empty URL expression (no empty-`to` node); matchHttpClient module-rooted matches (fetch/axios.get/http.request) are unaffected.
Existing precision tests (cross-method lexical scope, cross-class field scope) continue to pass unchanged under the same parse()->httpRels() harness.

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: the TS recognizer proves instance receivers from a body-wide flat `localHttp` set (collectLocalAxiosVars descends into nested closures, typescript.ts:713) and a module-level `currentClassHttpFields` that is switched only via extractClass (:304) — so a class DECLARED inside a method body (walked only by walkForCalls) inherits the outer class's this.<field> proof. The Python recognizer (collectPyProvenHttpReceivers, python.ts:330) collects every factory-assigned name into a flat set with no rebind handling. Net effect: three name-keyed false-positive cases — nested-closure shadow of an axios var, method-body-declared inner class, and Python same-function rebind — can emit spurious CALLS_HTTP.
migration.stateAfter: Receiver-proof resolves to the NEAREST lexical declaration: axios proofs are per-scope frames (a nested non-axios re-declaration shadows the outer proof; a plain outer-capture still resolves), currentClassHttpFields is saved/switched/restored when walkForCalls enters ANY class node (including one declared in a method body), and Python proofs follow last-binding-wins (a rebound name drops out). Strictly fewer CALLS_HTTP edges; all happy paths and existing precision tests unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Ship the recognizer changes (typescript.ts scope-frame axios resolution + inner-class save/restore; python.ts last-binding-wins) behind no flag — the parsers are pure functions invoked during indexing.

On next index / re-index of any affected source file, the parser naturally re-emits the narrowed CALLS_HTTP set for that file; stale false-positive edges from the prior heuristic are replaced during the normal per-file upsert. No manual backfill or bulk edge rewrite is required — coverage refreshes as files are re-parsed.
Optionally trigger a full re-index of repos that heavily use the affected patterns to purge any lingering pre-fix false-positive CALLS_HTTP edges immediately rather than on next file touch.

migration.backwardCompat: All four functions are module-internal (surfaceLevel internal); no exported/public API changes shape. walkForCalls's private param changes from `localHttp: Set<string>` to an axios scope stack — internal only, no external caller. The CALLS_HTTP relation shape (kind/from/to/resolved/meta) is unchanged, so downstream graph consumers and stored edges remain format-compatible; the only observable difference is fewer spurious edges. Reverting the commit fully restores prior behaviour.

alternativesConsidered.name: Lexical proof-frame stack in the walk
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Turn the two flat name-sets into a stack of proof frames pushed/popped as walkForCalls descends into each new lexical scope; a receiver resolves against the nearest frame.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Rank 2: correct-by-construction and removes the module-level mutable, but M-cost and a walkForCalls rewrite over-scope a 2-MED-1-LOW fix; scored only 'partial' on regression-safety and does not unify the Python path anyway.

alternativesConsidered.name: Targeted shadow/rebind subtraction at scope boundaries
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the current flat-set design but subtract proofs where a nearer binding overrides them: closure-local shadow kills, inner-class clear, Python same-function rebind drop.

alternativesConsidered.name: Full per-scope symbol table with binding kinds
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a proper scoped symbol table (binding name -> kind: httpClient | other) for each parsed file and resolve every receiver against it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Rank 3: 'violates' regression-safety — a new symbol-resolution subsystem far exceeds the story's small size, and tree-sitter carries no type info so the httpClient binding kind stays heuristic (negligible precision gain over a2).
